title: RuleForge: curated per-customer policy curation and staged apply for batching & KV-cache
creator: Leah Kim
description: Implement a RuleForge subsystem that automatically generates and curates per-customer and per-route optimization policies (batching aggressiveness, prefix/KV cache allowlists/denylists, quantization profile hints) and performs staged, observable config applies with automated rollback triggers. This ticket covers the curation ruleset, scoring heuristics, CI dry-run simulation harness, and the staged apply orchestration (canary percentages, telemetry gates, and emergency rollback path).
acceptance_criteria: RuleForge can generate an actionable policy JSON for a given customer+route that includes batching window, kv_cache_allowlist, kv_cache_denylist, and target_quant_profile
A dry-run simulation (sandbox) produces estimated token-cost delta, tail-latency impact, and cache hit-rate delta and writes results to the staging telemetry dashboard
Staged apply flow performs 3-step rollout (1%, 10%, 100%) with configurable hold gates based on cost, p95 latency, and error-rate thresholds
Automatic rollback triggers if any gate breaches thresholds within a hold window and rollback completes within SLOs with an audit entry
Integration tests validate policy generation for at least 5 customer archetypes (low-volume chat, high-throughput embeddings, mixed-burst API)
decisions: Use a hybrid scoring model: deterministic heuristics (safety-first rules) + lightweight ML ranker for cost-benefit where sufficient telemetry exists
Allowlist entries are authoritative for hot-prefix retention; denylist entries are scoped to routes and cannot override customer-level allowlist
Default rollout pattern is 1% -> 10% -> 100% with 30m hold windows, adjustable per-customer via release policy
All policy applies must be schema-validated and run through the dry-run simulation before any staged apply is permitted
notes: Focus on minimizing false positives that would hurt quality: conservative initial batch-window increases and prefer cache allowlists over aggressive global eviction policies
We will ship with an opt-out flag for enterprise customers and a review workflow for customers with audit requirements
Coordinate with Console team for visibility: per-policy diff view and per-canary telemetry charting

rollout_plan: Step 1: Dry-run simulation on 100% of traffic in sandbox project (no config mutate) - duration 24h
Step 2: Canary apply to 1% of production traffic, hold 30m, evaluate gates (cost delta, p95 latency delta, error-rate).
Step 3: If gates pass, expand to 10%, hold 1h, re-evaluate. If pass, full rollout to 100% with post-apply monitoring for 24h.
Step 4: For high-risk customers (enterprise tier), require manual approval before Step 2
rollback_plan: Automatic rollback when any gate breaches: immediate revert of policy with a tagged audit event
Emergency abort: set route-feature-flag to 'suspended' and route to fallback runtime variant
Post-rollback diagnostics job that runs the dry-run repro and collects traces for triage
test_plan: Unit tests for policy generator rules and schema validation
Integration tests for the staged apply state machine (simulate gate pass/fail scenarios)
E2E dry-run acceptance test that validates telemetry outputs match simulation expectations
